results.title: Traditional music teachers exploited authority to sexually abuse students: Court records
results.content: Sex crimes in the traditional Korean music community persist, fueled by the enormous influence teachers wield over students’ future careers and the close-knit, insular nature of the industry. Following the Hankook Ilbo’s in-depth coverage of sexual exploitation in the traditional music scene, victims continued to come forward with accounts of widespread sexual harassment and assault. Court rulings also revealed disturbing details of the crimes. An analysis by the Hankook Ilbo of court rulings from 2010 to 2026 involving sexual offenses committed by traditional music instructors who abused their positions of authority over students found that seven of the 11 cases involved underage victims. In four of those cases, the victims were younger than 13. results.title: Unwanted ballots worry Korean green card holders amid US voting crackdown
results.content: SEATTLE — With the Trump administration stepping up its crackdown on noncitizen voting ahead of Tuesday's midterm elections, some Korean green card holders are worried that receiving election ballots they never requested could land them in immigration trouble. Across online forums and social media discussions, including Korean-American communities, green card holders have shared accounts of receiving ballots or voter-registration materials despite not being U.S. citizens. "I'm a green card holder, but ballots come to my house every time," one user wrote. Another said she and her husband, both green card holders, had received jury summonses, and that her husband had also received election-related mail. results.title: Binance clients pull $4.7 billion after hack as crypto world studies fallout
results.content: SINGAPORE/PARIS — Binance's customers have withdrawn a net $4.72 billion from the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange since it reopened, after hackers stole around $6.3 billion of crypto from the platform in what could be the largest financial heist in history. The exchange froze withdrawals for about 48 hours after the hack, which which the FBI said was carried out by North Korea, then started allowing customers to withdraw again on Sunday morning. The theft has underlined the vulnerability of digital assets to attacks and raised questions about the impact on Binance, which has vowed to repay customers in full, and on the wider market. Binance said the net outflows amounted to around 3% of assets on the platform, a relatively modest figure that analysts said suggested customer confidence had largely held up. results.title: Personal information of Lee, presidential staff leaked: report
results.content: Personal information of President Lee Jae Myung and presidential staff has been leaked, a local broadcaster reported Monday, with the presidential office saying it had already taken measures in response. According to KBS, the personal information of 168 people, including Lee, staff from Cheong Wa Dae and the foreign ministry, along with reporters covering the presidential office, was posted on a website in a file titled "List of passengers (Republic of Korea-Belgium)." The Republic of Korea is the official name of South Korea. The list appeared related to passengers who traveled aboard the presidential plane during Lee's trip to Belgium, Italy and France in June. KBS reported that the file was available for download and was even posted on June 2 ahead of Lee's trip.
